headline: Will we get back together?
note:
🔄 REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 to the Natural Tarot-Cut framework. Bubbles 3-6 run as ONE causal chain — so / and / but / that's why — and the read ANSWERS. The art line and the bridge are unchanged. Every ban in this note still stands.

Face-down only (return-mhf). The US-FRAMED sibling of `reunion`, and that pairing is the whole experiment — reunion casts him as the agent and her as the one waiting; these cast the relationship as a joint thing with two people in it.

🔴 THE FORBIDDEN VERDICT IS ON THE RELATIONSHIP, NOT ON HIM — harder, not softer. A claim about a man can at least be measured against his behaviour; 'it is over' or 'it is not over' is unfalsifiable to her and lands as a ruling on her life from someone who has never met either of them. 🔴 NO ODDS — cards-still-a-chance asks for a number outright and there is none; no percentage, no 'strong chance', no 'likely'. 🔴 NO DIRECTIVES in either direction: move on, let go, fight for him, reach out first are all out. 🔴 Never hand her the outcome ('it is up to you', 'if you had only') — the us-framing makes that easy and it lands as blame.

Finding, and the one that is truest to the us-framing: this question is about a JOINT thing and only one of the two people is in the room. She has been carrying a two-person decision on her own — which is why it will not resolve however long she turns it over.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — his right arm is raised higher than the top of his head.
You came asking about getting back together. Your hand went to the man working alone.
So this isn't finished, dear. The card won't let me call it that.
And on that table, dear, one pair of hands does all the work.
But a thing like this takes two, dear, and only you have been working it.
That's why nothing moves, however hard you push. You've been the only one pushing.
Let me look closer at what has been keeping this a one-person job…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — his tied leg is straight, and the rope is short.
Your question was about getting back together. Your hand went to the card that holds the middle.
So you've been living in the middle of this, dear. It has no floor.
And look at him. Neither down nor up, and quite still.
But the middle is a place two people leave together, dear.
That's why you keep nearly getting out, dear, and end up back in it.
Let me look closer at what has been holding you in the middle…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — the stick over his shoulder is long and thin.
You asked about the road back together. Your hand went to the one who set out alone.
So the road back is still there, dear. Nobody has closed it.
And look at him. One road, one traveller, no second pair of boots.
But a road back needs two people walking it, dear.
That's why rest doesn't fix it, dear. You walked both parts of this.
Let me look closer at what has been standing on the road back…
